original_question: For the Veronese embedding of projective space P^n defined by O_{P^n}(d), Ottaviani and Paoletti prove that Property (N_k) fails when k >= 3d - 2. Is the complementary sharp positive statement true, namely that O_{P^n}(d) satisfies Property (N_p) for every p < 3d - 2?
target_in_paper: Introduction, Theorem G together with footnote 2: the Ottaviani-Paoletti conjectural converse to the failure bound k >= 3d - 2 for the d-uple Veronese embedding. In the paper's own formal syzygy language, this sits inside §2 as the b = 0 specialization of the Veronese discussion around Theorem 2.1, Example 2.2, and Conjecture 2.3, with Property (N_p) translated into Koszul-cohomology vanishing by Example 1.4.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant geometric object (the Veronese embedding of projective space via O_{P^n}(d)), the Ottaviani-Paoletti failure threshold 3d - 2, and the intended complementary positive statement 'Property (N_p) for p < 3d - 2'. This is indeed the narrow statement singled out in the paper, via the remark that Ottaviani-Paoletti conjectured this converse and proved it for P^2.
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers, so the ambient variety is P^n_C.
The intended embedding should be stated explicitly as the d-uple Veronese embedding defined by the complete linear series |O_{P^n}(d)|.
The integer quantifiers should be explicit: n >= 2 is the intended higher-dimensional setting here, d is a positive integer, and p is an integer with 0 <= p < 3d - 2.
Property (N_p) should be defined, not just named: projective normality plus linearity of the first p steps of the minimal graded free resolution.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify the graded ring and resolution: S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)) and R = ⊕_{m >= 0} H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(md)).
The draft does not mention that the paper attributes the complementary statement to Ottaviani-Paoletti and notes that they proved it when n = 2.
The paper's internal reformulation uses Koszul cohomology K_{p,q}; the draft omits this equivalent language supplied by Definition 1.2 and Example 1.4.
The draft does not indicate that the paper's broader formal generalization is Conjecture 2.3 for K_{p,q}(n,b;d), of which your question is only the special b = 0, Property (N_p) slice.
refined_question: Over C, fix integers n >= 2 and d >= 1, let S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)), and let R = ⊕_{m >= 0} H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(md)) be the homogeneous coordinate ring of the d-uple Veronese embedding nu_d: P^n -> P(H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d))^*). Is it true that for every integer p with 0 <= p < 3d - 2, the minimal graded free resolution of R over S satisfies E_0 ≅ S and E_i ≅ ⊕ S(-i-1) for all 1 <= i <= p; equivalently, does O_{P^n}(d) satisfy Green-Lazarsfeld Property (N_p) for every p < 3d - 2?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each integer p with 0 <= p < 3d - 2, do the Koszul cohomology groups of the d-uple Veronese embedding satisfy K_{0,q}(P^n; O_{P^n}(d)) = 0 for all q != 0 and K_{i,q}(P^n; O_{P^n}(d)) = 0 for every 1 <= i <= p and every q != 1?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's narrow Ottaviani-Paoletti converse, not at the broader asymptotic nonvanishing problem of §1. In the Introduction, the paper states Theorem G: Property (N_k) fails for O_{P^n}(d) when k >= 3d - 2, and immediately adds in footnote 2 that Ottaviani-Paoletti 'also conjecture - and prove in the case of P^2 - that (N_p) holds for p < 3d - 2.' That is the closest official formulation to your draft. Section 2 then explains why 3d - 2 is the relevant threshold in the Veronese setting: Theorem 2.1 gives the nonvanishing range for K_{p,q}(n,b;d), Example 2.2 specializes this to K_{p,2}(P^2; O_{P^2}(d)) != 0 for p >= 3d - 2, and Conjecture 2.3 predicts vanishing outside the stated range. Example 1.4 is the paper's explicit equivalence between Property (N_p) and Koszul-cohomology vanishing, so it supplies the only legitimate alternate formulation.
